title: Horizontal machine-tool slide hydraulic requirements
scope_statement: Validated scope: generic hydraulic component classes, functional valve behavior, and direct port-to-port connectivity only. Pump/cylinder/reservoir sizing, pressure and flow ratings, line selection, filtration, cooling, prime mover selection, simulation and fabrication approval are explicitly deferred to the later sizing and engineering phases.
design_narrative: Open-circuit fixed-displacement hydraulic slide circuit. Tank supplies Pump suction. Pump pressure branches directly to the main ReliefValve and the tandem-center 4/3 DCV. ReliefValve.T and DCV.T return directly to Tank.R. DCV.A feeds the cylinder cap end for extension. The cylinder rod side and DCV.B are connected through two parallel legs: a pressure-compensated one-way flow control in the rod-exhaust A-to-B direction for cutting feed, and a position-operated bypass around it for rapid approach and unmetered retract. During rapid approach the DCV is in extend and the bypass is open; during cutting feed the DCV remains in extend and the bypass is closed so rod-end exhaust is forced through the pressure-compensated flow control; during retract the DCV is in retract and the bypass is open for an unrestricted rod-side supply path while cap-end exhaust returns through DCV.A to tank.

motion_control_decisions.justification: Approach is the faster phase in the same extend direction before a slower controlled feed; horizontal load is resistive and no holding or overrunning condition is stated.

Cutting feed speed is adjustable and must remain materially unchanged with ±15% cutting-load variation; for a horizontal resistive extend feed requiring deliberate throttling, meter-out of rod exhaust is the conventional inferred metering side.
Retract has only a maximum time requirement and a resistive horizontal load; no deliberate speed-control behavior or holding requirement is stated.

Provides the unrestricted parallel path around FeedFlowControl for rapid approach before the 250 mm trip.

phase_configurations.notes: Rod-end exhaust path is SlideCylinder.Rod -> RapidFeedBypass.P -> RapidFeedBypass.A -> DCV.B -> DCV.T -> Tank.R; the open bypass prevents feed throttling in this rapid phase.

component_states.reason: Maintains cap-end supply and rod-end exhaust for the cutting feed stroke.

phase_configurations.notes: Metered rod-exhaust path is SlideCylinder.Rod -> FeedFlowControl.A -> FeedFlowControl.B -> DCV.B -> DCV.T -> Tank.R with no simultaneously open unmetered bypass.

component_states.reason: Connects P to B and A to T so the rod end is supplied and the cap end exhausts to tank.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power, relief, and return manifold-free supply
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: Tank provides the open-circuit suction boundary through Tank.S to Pump.S, and Pump supplies hydraulic flow from Pump.P to the pressure branch.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Open-circuit power, relief, and return manifold-free supply
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: ReliefValve is connected directly from Pump.P pressure to Tank.R return through ReliefValve.P and ReliefValve.T; its numerical relief setting is deferred to sizing/commissioning and must be no higher than 70 bar.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Double-acting slide cylinder with 4-way directional control
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: DCV extend and retract states pressurize the cap or rod chamber of the double-acting SlideCylinder. DCV neutral unloads Pump.P to Tank.R while blocking A and B for a stationary tandem-center neutral condition.

function_implementations.circuit_pattern: Position-operated rapid-approach / pressure-compensated feed / rapid-retract rod-side bypass
function_implementations.how_requirements_met: RapidFeedBypass and FeedFlowControl form parallel legs between the cylinder rod node and DCV.B. Bypass open gives rapid approach; bypass closed at the position trip forces rod exhaust through FeedFlowControl for controlled cutting feed; bypass open during retract gives an unmetered return path.
FeedFlowControl meters the rod-side exhaust in its pressure-compensated A-to-B direction during cutting-feed extension, implementing the declared load-independent adjustable meter-out decision.
Only one actuator is present, so no synchronization component or cross-connection is required.
No pilot check, counterbalance valve, or dual load lock is selected because the load is horizontal/resistive and no holding, no-drift, hose-burst, or overrunning requirement is stated.

design_decisions.decision: Selected a fixed-pump open-circuit supply with one tank, one fixed-displacement pump, and one main relief valve.
design_decisions.rationale: The open-circuit pattern satisfies the required hydraulic supply and provides a direct pressure-relief path to tank without adding manifolds or tee components.

design_decisions.decision: Used a tandem-center 4/3 DCV for the single double-acting slide cylinder.
design_decisions.rationale: The DCV provides extend, retract, and neutral unloading behavior suitable for a fixed-displacement pump; the selected circuit has no load-lock requirement that would require a float/open-center pairing with pilot-operated checks.

design_decisions.decision: Placed the pressure-compensated one-way flow control only in the rod-side exhaust path for extend cutting feed.
design_decisions.rationale: This directly implements the immutable motion-control decision: cutting feed is pressure-compensated, load-independent, rod-chamber meter-out on exhaust during extension.

design_decisions.decision: Connected the position-operated bypass in parallel around the feed-control leg and changed its state by phase.
design_decisions.rationale: The bypass is open for unrestricted rapid approach, closed for controlled feed so it cannot defeat metering, and open for unmetered retract.

design_decisions.decision: Did not add check valves, sequence valves, counterbalance valves, pilot checks, or separate approach/return flow controls.
design_decisions.rationale: The typed motion decisions require only unrestricted rapid, one controlled feed meter-out path, and sizing-only retract for a resistive horizontal load; adding extra functional valves would introduce unrequested behavior and hardware.

assumptions: Relief-valve pressure setting, cylinder dimensions, pump flow, feed adjustment calibration, and position-trip hardware are deferred to sizing and commissioning.
RapidFeedBypass is reset or commanded by its mechanical position arrangement to be open for retract; the FeedFlowControl also provides free reverse B-to-A flow if bypass reset timing is imperfect.
Branching is represented only by repeated component ports, not by tee, hose, line, or manifold components.
No electrical or mechanical-drive external interfaces are emitted because solenoid and position actuation are properties of the selected generic classes.
open_issues: Confirm during implementation that the position operator resets or reopens for retract, or rely on the catalog flow-control free reverse path for unmetered rod-end supply.
Relief setting, cylinder dimensions, pump flow, feed adjustment calibration, and trip position hardware are deferred to sizing and commissioning.

research_coverage.summary: Evidence is sufficient for the basic open-circuit power/return/relief topology and for double-acting cylinder directional control with safe neutral behavior. Evidence is also good for generic meter-out speed control and for a rapid/feed bypass assembly concept. However, two critical claims remain under-supported: pressure-compensated flow control as the basis for load-independent feed speed under changing cutting load, and automatic position-based transition from rapid approach to slow feed without stopping. Because these are critical required behaviors, the design cannot proceed without targeted follow-up evidence.

items.rationale: Findings provide cited engineering guidance for reservoir-to-pump suction, pump outlet pressure supply, return-to-reservoir path, and relief valve connected from pressure side to tank/reservoir for overpressure protection. Citations include LibreTexts and Power & Motion technical material with verified excerpts on pump outlet pressure, return line to reservoir, relief opening at set pressure, and diverting excess flow to reservoir/tank.

Findings support a double-acting cylinder controlled by one 3-position, 4-way DCV, with A-to-cap/B-to-rod hookup, P→A/B→T extension, P→B/A→T retraction, and neutral stop/hold behavior. Evidence includes LibreTexts and Power & Motion technical citations; the tandem-center neutral detail is supported by a lower-quality source but is consistent with the primary DCV evidence and adequate for topology selection.

The rapid approach / slow feed / return concept is partially supported. T3 supports meter-out speed control on actuator exhaust and rod-end pressure-compensated flow-control placement; T4 supports a 2-way, 2-position rapid/feed bypass concept with full-flow rapid motion and diverted flow through a flow-control valve for controlled feed. However, the accumulated findings themselves note that they do not directly verify a position-operated changeover at a fixed slide trip point, uninterrupted transition without stopping, or explicit load-independent behavior from pressure compensation. These are essential to the specified multi-phase motion profile.

Sources identify pressure-compensated flow-control components and rod-end placement, but the evidence does not explicitly support the key engineering claim that pressure compensation maintains substantially constant flow/feed speed despite load-induced pressure variation. Since cutting-load variation is a critical driver requirement, component presence alone is not enough.

T4 supports a rapid-advance/feed circuit using a 2-way, 2-position valve that allows full flow when open and diverts through a flow-control valve when closed. It does not directly support automatic position-based switching at the 250 mm trip point or continuous rapid-to-feed transition without stopping. The bin95 source appears promising because it lists 'Rapid Traverse and Feed Using Deceleration Valve,' but the relevant circuit details were not extracted.

missing_or_weak_information: Missing explicit technical evidence that a pressure-compensated hydraulic flow-control valve maintains near-constant flow, and therefore actuator feed speed, despite changes in load/pressure differential.

Missing circuit-level evidence for automatic position-operated rapid-to-feed changeover, such as a mechanically actuated deceleration valve or limit-operated 2/2 bypass valve tripped by the slide at the approach/feed boundary.
Missing explicit support that the rapid-to-feed transition can occur without stopping, or enough connection/sequence detail to infer uninterrupted changeover safely.

Motion-profile evidence should confirm that any bypass/check arrangement provides unrestricted rapid approach and return/retraction while forcing rod-side exhaust through the metering element only during cutting-feed extension.

design_review.summary: The topology functionally satisfies the brief: open-circuit tank/pump/relief supply is direct, the 4/3 DCV provides extend and retract paths for the single double-acting slide cylinder, the rod-side exhaust during cutting feed is forced through exactly one pressure-compensated meter-out flow control, and the position-operated bypass is correctly open for rapid approach, closed for controlled feed, and reopened for retract. No blocking functional, safety, sequencing, metering, or topology-prohibition issues were found.

validation.summary: Deterministic validation: valid. Engineering review: valid. The topology functionally satisfies the brief: open-circuit tank/pump/relief supply is direct, the 4/3 DCV provides extend and retract paths for the single double-acting slide cylinder, the rod-side exhaust during cutting feed is forced through exactly one pressure-compensated meter-out flow control, and the position-operated bypass is correctly open for rapid approach, closed for controlled feed, and reopened for retract. No blocking functional, safety, sequencing, metering, or topology-prohibition issues were found.

policy.approach: Smallest verified design: ISO-100 cylinder, conventional rod, smallest standard fixed pump that clears rapid approach and return.

actuator_decisions.justification: The cutting-feed extension phase is the governing load phase. area_for_force at this pressure returned 6880.3 mm2 for the governing force input used, and choose_bore selected 100 mm with 7854.0 mm2. choose_rod with force strategy selected a 56 mm rod, 5391.0 mm2 annulus, and 1.457 area ratio.

supply_decision.justification: flow_for_speed returned 23.562 L/min for the approach requirement on the 7854.0 mm2 cap area, and choose_pump selected 19.0 cm3/rev delivering 25.65 L/min. The same pump was verified for the 5391.0 mm2 annulus retract requirement.

setting_decisions.basis: The setting is at the listed system pressure ceiling; evaluate_sizing_policy proved all seven acceptance checks with worst reported operating pressure below the setting.
